family: your whole money goes to the thing itself
why: Someone else already paid the part nobody wants to pay.
for_client: Furniture maker's sponsor day: 'Our supplier has paid all the workshop costs this week: every euro goes into your table's wood.' (only if true)
source: Gneezy, Keenan, Gneezy, Avoiding overhead aversion in charity, Science 2014

opening: Make one gift now and we'll never ask for another donation again.
picture: envelope with photographs of children with clefts and the headline
beat: Smile Train's own best control packages after years of testing
result: 0.66% vs 0.34% gave (+93% donors); $56 vs $50 gift; $152,928 vs $71,566 (+114%); later gifts equal ($107,855 vs $107,043); nearly 50% more in total
measured_by: Five mailing waves; 415,226 households got the line
family: we will never ask again
why: It is against the sender's interest and frees the reader; he gives back once for the kindness.
for_client: Newsletter of a garden centre: 'Tell us once what you grow. We will never ask again.' Car servicing: 'One call. We won't ring you again.'
source: Kamdar, Levitt, List, Mullaney, Syverson, Once and Done, working paper 2015

opening: Letter naming the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation as the giver who doubles the reader's gift ($2 for each $1)
beat: the same match from an unnamed donor (experiment 2); no match (experiment 1)
result: naming the giver: +51% money per letter; against no match: +81% money and +79% donors
measured_by: Two randomised mailings (prior donors; cold lists)
family: a name you trust has already put its own money in
why: The careful giver's money says the thing is good.
for_client: New baby food: 'The city's children's hospital already buys it for its wards' — the named buyer first (true only)
source: Karlan & List, How Can Bill and Melinda Gates Increase Other People's Donations, 2012
doubt: The letter's own words are not printed in the passage read; N in the paper's tables

opening: We had another member, they contributed $300. How much would you like to pledge today?
beat: no mention; $75; $180
result: average $119.70 vs about $106.72 (+12%); first-time givers +29% ($25.33)
measured_by: Field experiment, 538 callers; the named gifts were real
family: what another person just did
why: A real, fairly high example sets what is normal for a newcomer.
for_client: Caterer on the phone: 'The last school we did took the 40-person table. How many are you?' (real case)
source: Shang & Croson, A Field Experiment in Charitable Contribution, 2006 version (Economic Journal 2009)
doubt: No effect on renewing members; $75 and $180 not significant; a low example can lower gifts (Costa Rica park)

opening: A table plaque with the five most popular dishes, by number of dishes sold in the previous week
picture: small plaque on the table listing five dish names
seller: Mei Zhou Dong Po — Sichuan restaurant chain, Beijing
beat: no plaque; a plaque with five 'sample dishes' (names only)
result: demand for the five dishes +13 to 18%; a plaque that only names dishes: no significant effect
measured_by: Randomised field experiment, 13 sites, tables randomised
family: most ordered last week
why: Others' real choices are information; mere mention is not.
for_client: Hardware shop shelf card: 'Five most bought here last week' with the five items
source: Cai, Chen, Fang, Observational Learning, NBER 13516 (AER 2009)

opening: Hello, I am a professor at Harvard studying the opinions, decision-making, goals, and expectations of school board members. I would like to learn from you how school district leaders are thinking about the challenges facing schools right now. Would you please complete this brief survey?
seller: Harvard researcher — survey request to school board members
beat: the same e-mail with the flattery and reasons left in (127 words)
result: 4.8% answered vs 2.7% (+78%); 49 words vs 127
measured_by: Randomised, 7,002 school board members
family: who I am, what I want, done
why: Readers judge by length how much work the request is.
for_client: Event caterer to schools: 'Hello, I cook for school fairs in Leeds. Could you tell me your date? It takes one line.'
source: Rogers & Lasky-Fink, When Writing for Busy Readers, Less Is More, Behavioral Scientist, 2023

opening: Cumberland-Spiced Veggie Sausage & Mash
beat: Meat-Free Sausage and Mash
result: sales +76%
measured_by: Sainsbury's / WRI Better Buying Lab, August-October 2017; N not given
family: place and taste instead of what is missing
why: It names where the taste comes from; the old name named an absence.
for_client: Sugar-free bakery: 'Sicilian Almond Biscuit' instead of 'Sugar-free biscuit'
source: World Resources Institute (Better Buying Lab), It's All in a Name: How to Boost the Sales of Plant-Based Menu Items, 2019

opening: Cuban Black Bean Soup
seller: Panera Bread — menu name, 18 Los Angeles cafes
beat: Low Fat Vegetarian Black Bean Soup
result: sales +13%
measured_by: Month-long naming test, January 2018; N not given
family: place and taste instead of what is missing
why: The origin promises flavour; 'low fat' promises none.
for_client: Massage studio: 'Forest-pine back massage' instead of 'Hypoallergenic massage'
source: World Resources Institute (Better Buying Lab), It's All in a Name: How to Boost the Sales of Plant-Based Menu Items, 2019

opening: Field Grown Breakfast
beat: Meat-free Breakfast (and Garden Breakfast +12%)
result: sales +17%
measured_by: Sainsbury's / WRI Better Buying Lab; N not given
family: where it grew
why: The eater sees the field; the old name saw no meat.
for_client: Juice bar: 'Orchard Press' instead of 'No-added-sugar juice'
source: World Resources Institute (Better Buying Lab), It's All in a Name: How to Boost the Sales of Plant-Based Menu Items, 2019

opening: Garden Breakfast
beat: Meat-free Breakfast
result: sales +12%
measured_by: Sainsbury's / WRI Better Buying Lab; N not given
family: where it grew
why: Warm place word instead of a lack.
for_client: Florist-cafe: 'Greenhouse lunch' instead of 'vegan lunch'
source: World Resources Institute (Better Buying Lab), It's All in a Name: How to Boost the Sales of Plant-Based Menu Items, 2019

opening: Rich Buttery Roasted Sweet Corn / Zesty Ginger Turmeric Sweet Potatoes
beat: healthy-restrictive labels; basic labels, for the identical dish
result: chosen 41% more often than under 'healthy restrictive' names, 25% more than under plain names
measured_by: Turnwald, Boles, Crum, JAMA Internal Medicine 2017, as reported by WRI; N not given there
family: say the taste, not the virtue
why: People choose by expected pleasure.
for_client: Toothpaste for children: 'Crushed strawberry foam' instead of 'Fluoride cavity protection'
source: World Resources Institute (Better Buying Lab), It's All in a Name: How to Boost the Sales of Plant-Based Menu Items, 2019

opening: Herb n’ Honey Balsamic Glazed Turnips
seller: US university dining halls — dish label
beat: Healthy Choice Turnips; Turnips
result: taste labels: +29% chosen against health labels, +14% against plain; +39% eaten by weight against health labels
measured_by: Preregistered multi-site trial, 5 universities, 137,842 diner decisions, 185 days, 24 vegetables
family: say the taste, not the virtue
why: Expected pleasure; works best where the food really tastes good.
for_client: Bakery: 'Toasted walnut and date rye' instead of 'High-fibre rye'
source: Turnwald et al., Increasing Vegetable Intake by Emphasizing Tasty and Enjoyable Attributes, Psychological Science 2019

opening: Sizzlin’ Szechuan Green Beans with Toasted Garlic
seller: US university dining halls — dish label
beat: Nutritious Green Beans; Green Beans
result: see pooled result: +29% against health labels, +14% against plain
measured_by: 5 universities, 137,842 diner decisions
family: say the taste, not the virtue
why: Sound, place and roasted flavour in six words.
for_client: Candle maker: 'Crackling cedar and burnt orange' instead of 'Natural soy candle'
source: Turnwald et al., Increasing Vegetable Intake by Emphasizing Tasty and Enjoyable Attributes, Psychological Science 2019

opening: Twisted Citrus Glazed Carrots
seller: US university dining halls — dish label
beat: health-focused label; 'Carrots'
result: pooled: +29% against health labels, +14% against plain
measured_by: 5 universities, 137,842 diner decisions
family: say the taste, not the virtue
why: A preparation and a flavour, true to the dish.
for_client: Deli: 'Slow-fired lemon chickpeas' instead of 'Protein chickpeas'
source: Turnwald et al., Increasing Vegetable Intake by Emphasizing Tasty and Enjoyable Attributes, Psychological Science 2019

opening: Previous Gift: <date>  (bold line above 'Dear Friend and Supporter')
picture: bold line between the address and the greeting with the date of the reader's own last gift
seller: American Red Cross — appeal to past donors
beat: the same letter without the line
measured_by: Randomised, N = 17,061
family: you did this on this date
why: It shows the reader he is already someone who does it.
for_client: Piano tuner: 'Last tuned: 12 March 2025' in bold above 'Dear Mrs Roy'
source: Kessler & Milkman, Identity in Charitable Giving, Management Science 64(2), 2018

opening: [City name] Community Drive (e.g. 'New York Community Drive')
beat: [State] Drive (4.12%); Annual Drive (4.01%); Winter Drive (3.82%)
result: 5.51% gave vs 4.12% / 4.01% / 3.82% (+34% on the best rival); money per letter +4.8 log points, gift of each giver 13% lower
measured_by: Randomised, about 41,400 letters
family: named after the reader's town
why: The town is part of who he is; strongest in small towns.
for_client: Solar installer: 'Harrogate Roof Week' instead of 'Summer Solar Campaign'
source: Kessler & Milkman, Identity in Charitable Giving, Management Science 64(2), 2018

opening: Did you know that working off a bottle of soda or fruit juice takes about 5 miles of walking?
picture: brightly coloured sign on the drinks case
seller: Baltimore corner stores — sign on the beverage case
beat: no sign; '... has about 250 calories?'; '... about 16 teaspoons of sugar?'; '... about 50 minutes of running?' (201 kcal)
result: any sign: calories bought 149 -> 121 (all purchases); the walking sign fewest calories among sugary drinks bought, 190 vs 201 kcal for running (P = .009); still lower after signs came down
measured_by: 6 stores, 4,516 purchases, signs in random order
family: did you know + the sum turned into steps
why: A number nobody could feel is turned into effort everybody knows.
for_client: Window firm: 'Did you know the gap under this door loses the heat of 5 full kettles a day?' (measured)
source: Bleich et al., Reducing Sugar-Sweetened Beverage Consumption by Providing Caloric Information, AJPH 2014
doubt: Differences among the signs are modest; before/after without control stores

opening: Hi, how are you? Merry Christmas. Please give today.
picture: bell-ringer looks the passer-by in the eye
seller: Salvation Army — bell-ringers at a supermarket door
beat: bell only, silent, no eye contact
result: givers +55%, money +69% (one door); +53% givers, +45% money (two doors); but about a third of shoppers avoided the asked door
measured_by: Randomised natural field experiment, Boston area supermarket
family: look, greet, ask plainly
why: The plain spoken ask with eye contact moves people; it also makes some walk away.
for_client: Market stall: 'Morning! Would you like a slice of the new cheddar?' with eye contact, instead of a silent tray
source: Andreoni, Rao, Trachtman, Avoiding the Ask, NBER 17648 (J. Political Economy 2017)

opening: TV, radio and newspaper advertisements: switch from whole and 2% milk to 1% or less
seller: 1% or Less campaign, Wheeling, West Virginia
beat: comparison city without the campaign; before the campaign
result: low-fat milk 18% -> 41% of milk sales the month after, held at six months; total milk sales +16%
measured_by: Supermarket sales data in intervention and comparison communities
family: one small exact change
why: Not 'eat healthier' but one carton for another at the shelf.
for_client: Electrician: 'Swap one bulb: the one over your stove' instead of 'Save energy at home'
source: Reger, Wootan, Booth-Butterfield, Smith, 1% or Less: a community-based nutrition campaign, Public Health Reports 1998 (abstract)
doubt: The exact advertisement wording is not in the abstract; campaign of six weeks with several media

opening: The New Year as a fresh start, the three steps needed, and act now or lose the chance to contribute (redesigned e-mail of 2 January)
seller: US Department of Defense — Thrift Savings Plan re-enrolment
beat: the standard informational e-mail
result: 28.7% re-enrolled vs 23.5% in one week (+22%, 3,770 more people)
measured_by: Randomised by ID digits, N = 139,273
family: fresh start day, three steps, what you lose
why: A date that feels like a beginning and a short list.
for_client: Gym on 1 September: 'New school year, new hour for you. Three steps: pick a class, bring shoes, come Monday.'
source: Social and Behavioral Sciences Team, 2015 Annual Report (White House)
doubt: Wording described in the report, e-mail shown only as a picture

opening: ... at least 1 percent of your pay (e-mail naming the smallest contribution, 1%)
seller: US Department of Defense — Thrift Savings Plan
beat: e-mails naming 2 to 8 percent; an e-mail naming no rate; no e-mail
result: highest enrolment, 3.0%, for the e-mail naming 1%
measured_by: Randomised, n = 699,674
family: the smallest first step
why: The first step is so small that it is hard to refuse.
for_client: Language school: 'Start with one lesson' instead of 'Our 24-lesson course'
source: Social and Behavioral Sciences Team, 2016 Annual Report (White House)
doubt: E-mail's exact words not printed in the passage read

opening: Please Read: An Urgent Appeal from Wikipedia Founder Jimmy Wales
picture: plain white banner with Jimmy Wales's face and a small 'Read now' button
beat: hundreds of other banner messages tested from August to December 2010; editors' banners: same clicks, about half the gifts
result: unbeaten all campaign until the last days of the year
measured_by: Wikimedia Foundation, live A/B tests on Wikipedia
family: a person asks you to read
why: A named human, a plea, and nothing sold in the banner.
for_client: Bookshop: 'Please read: a note from Ruth, who opened this shop in 1994'
source: Wikimedia Foundation, Fundraising 2010 Report

also.source: Wikimedia Foundation, Fundraising 2010 Banner testing
also.result: click-through 3.68%, 62 donations, $2,125.91; best rival 0.25%, 5 donations, $431.42

opening: If everyone reading this donated $5 our fundraiser would end today. Please donate to keep Wikipedia free.
beat: Please Read: An Urgent Appeal from Wikipedia Founder Jimmy Wales
result: beat the year's best banner in the last days of 2010; used again with success in December 2011
measured_by: Wikimedia Foundation live A/B tests
family: if everyone reading this ...
why: A tiny share for each, a total that ends the begging, and the reader included.
for_client: Village swimming club: 'If everyone reading this came once a month, the pool would stay open.' (true sum)
source: Wikimedia Foundation, Fundraising 2010 Report

opening: Only 4 days left in 2010 to make a tax-deductible contribution to keep Wikipedia free. Please help Wikipedia pay its bills in 2011.
beat: Please Read: An Urgent Appeal from Wikipedia Founder Jimmy Wales
result: beat the year's best banner in the last days of 2010
measured_by: Wikimedia Foundation live A/B tests
family: true days left
why: A real date and a plain need: pay the bills.
for_client: Plumber: 'Only 4 days left to have the gas check before the landlord's certificate runs out'
source: Wikimedia Foundation, Fundraising 2010 Report

opening: I got a lot of funny looks ten years ago when I started talking to people about Wikipedia.
seller: Wikipedia — first line of the founder's appeal
beat: other first lines of the appeal, tested in the launch phase
result: the most successful appeal of the launch phase
measured_by: Wikimedia Foundation live A/B tests
family: they looked at me funny when I started
why: Founder's own small humiliation; everyone knows how it ended.
for_client: Bakery owner: 'My neighbours laughed when I dragged a stone oven into a garage.'
source: Wikimedia Foundation, Fundraising 2010 Report

opening: Banner with editor Susan Hewitt photographed in front of a tree in her garden (green leaves left in the picture)
picture: woman in front of green leaves; background not cut out
beat: Jimmy Wales on plain white
result: +64% clicks; green behind Jimmy's own photo also won
measured_by: Wikimedia Foundation live A/B test, then a control test with the same face
family: a home snapshot left as it is
why: It looked like a person's own photo, not a designed strip. [mine]
for_client: Tutor's ad: phone photo at the kitchen table with the plants in it, not a cut-out on white
source: Wikimedia Foundation, Fundraising 2011 Report

opening: The 'facts banner': the key facts about Wikipedia written in the banner itself, no click needed to read them
picture: a narrow strip of text at the top, no face
beat: the 'personal appeal' banner with the founder's photo
result: in some tests about three times as many donations; campaign fell from 46 days to 9
measured_by: Wikimedia Foundation, 10-20 live A/B tests a day
family: the whole case in the first box
why: The obstacle (a click) is gone; everybody reads the facts.
for_client: Roofer's ad image that carries the whole offer: 'Two men, one day, €390, ten-year paper, we take the rubble'
source: Wikimedia Foundation, Fundraising 2012 Report

opening: Dear Wikipedia reader
beat: the same facts banner without the salutation
measured_by: Wikimedia live A/B test, 25 November 2012, about 1 million impressions per arm as they noted it
family: a letter's salutation naming what you are doing now
why: The box becomes a letter to the person reading this page. [mine]
for_client: Recipe blog's knife offer: 'Dear person cooking tonight,'
source: Wikimedia Foundation fund-raising team, Fundraising 2012/We Need A Breakthrough (public test diary, May-November 2012)

opening: If Wikipedia is useful to you, please help keep it online another year.
beat: the control facts banner without the line
result: 826 gifts vs 711 (+16%), £13,826 vs £11,422; earlier small run 514 vs 466
measured_by: Wikimedia live A/B tests, 22 and 25 November 2012
family: if this is useful to you
why: The line was taken from what givers said when asked why they gave.
for_client: Local news site: 'If this street page is useful to you, help keep it printed another year.'
source: Wikimedia Foundation fund-raising team, Fundraising 2012/We Need A Breakthrough (public test diary, May-November 2012)

opening: Facts line: we take no government funds ('No government funds' banner)
beat: the line comparing Wikipedia with Google and Yahoo (their best fact for a year)
result: 1,680 gifts vs 1,520 (+11%); amount $17,488 vs $14,235 (gifts up to $18 column)
measured_by: Wikimedia live A/B test, 16 October 2012
family: who does NOT pay for us
why: It explains why the reader's money is needed and why he can trust it. [mine]
for_client: Review site: 'No brand has ever paid for a place on this list.' (only if true)
source: Wikimedia Foundation fund-raising team, Fundraising 2012/We Need A Breakthrough (public test diary, May-November 2012)
doubt: The banner's full text is only shown as a link

opening: (mailing promising to show the neighbours who voted and who did not, with the names and past voting printed on it)
beat: DO YOUR CIVIC DUTY - VOTE! (31.5%); no letter (29.7%); 'you are being studied' (32.2%); own household's record (34.5%)
result: 37.8% voted vs 29.7% with no letter (+8.1 points)
measured_by: Randomised, about 180,000 households; control 191,243 people
family: others will see
why: Being seen by people one knows moves more than duty.
for_client: Use only the gentle form: a shop board of neighbours who already signed up, each with consent
source: Gerber, Green, Larimer, Social Pressure and Voter Turnout, American Political Science Review 2008
doubt: Publishing private records is shaming; take only the mechanism with consent. The mailing is described in the paper, its headline is not printed in the text read

opening: Official electronic letter whose point is the possible heart benefit of the flu shot (cardiovascular gain letter)
beat: usual care (80.12%); seven other nudge letters that did not differ from usual care
result: 81.00% vs 80.12% (+0.89 point); repeated letter +0.73; strongest among those not vaccinated the year before
measured_by: Randomised nationwide trial, 964,870 people
family: a benefit you did not know it had
why: New, personal and bigger than the known benefit.
for_client: Dentist: 'Healthy gums, steadier blood sugar: what one cleaning does beyond your teeth' (only documented effects)
source: Johansen et al., Electronic nudges to increase influenza vaccination uptake in Denmark (NUDGE-FLU), The Lancet 2023 (abstract)
doubt: Small effect on a very high base; letter text not printed in the abstract

opening: [First name], ... (the reader's name at the start of the subject line)
beat: the same subject line without the name
result: opened 10.80% vs 9.05% (+20%); sales leads 0.51% vs 0.39% (+31%); unsubscribes 1.0% vs 1.2% (-17%)
measured_by: Randomised field experiments with sales e-mails of three companies, article page read (N not in the passage read)
family: own first name
why: The eye catches its own name; a wrong use would tire it. [mine]
for_client: Pet shop: 'Anna, Rex is due his tablets on Friday'
source: Sahni, Wheeler, Chintagunta, Personalization in Email Marketing, Marketing Science 2018

opening: If everyone reading this gave $5, the fundraiser would be done within an hour. Please help us forget fundraising and get back to Wikipedia.
beat: the same facts banner without the last sentence
measured_by: Wikimedia live A/B test, 1 October 2012; used to the end of the campaign
family: help us stop asking and go back to the thing itself
why: The asker would rather be doing the work; giving ends the interruption.
for_client: Theatre: 'If everyone here took one seat for a friend, the hall would be full tonight. Help us stop selling and start playing.'
source: Wikimedia Foundation fund-raising team, Fundraising 2012/We Need A Breakthrough (public test diary, May-November 2012)

opening: Facts banner with a blue-and-white top strip, the $5 line and 'get back to Wikipedia' (translated), against the older grey one
picture: blue strip, white text, three columns
beat: grey dropdown facts banner with image

source: Wikimedia Foundation fund-raising team, Fundraising 2012/We Need A Breakthrough (public test diary, May-November 2012)

beat: the same facts banner without the $5 line
result: 1,041 gifts vs 579 (+80%); $14,700 vs $11,500 (+28%); average gift lower

opening: Google might have close to a million servers. Yahoo has something like 12,000 staff. We have 679 servers and 138 employees.
beat: the same banner without the comparison
result: 293 gifts vs 218 in ten minutes (+34%); their note: a huge gain in 2011; retired later for 'no government funds' (+11% more)
measured_by: Wikimedia live A/B tests 2011-2012

why: Exact small numbers beside famous big ones make the work look amazing.

opening: You consumed more water than 73% of your Cobb County neighbors.
beat: tip sheet only (about -1%); tip sheet + appeal to do one's part
result: water use about 4.8% lower than control vs about 1% for tips alone; equal to a 12-15% price rise
measured_by: Natural field experiment, over 100,000 households
family: your own number against your neighbours'
why: A private exact rank among people next door.
for_client: Heating firm: 'Your boiler burned more gas than 73% of the homes in Elm Road.' (measured, private letter)
source: Ferraro & Price, Using Non-Pecuniary Strategies to Influence Behavior, NBER 17189 (REStat 2013)

opening: The Queen of Christmas Presents.
picture: a display rack of carpet sweepers with the card on it; letter told dealers racks and cards were free, as a reward for a signed promise to display
seller: Bissell Carpet Sweeper Company — carpet sweepers
beat: the company's only practice, road salesmen; the manager laughed at selling such dealers by letter
result: some five thousand letters brought one thousand orders, almost the first orders they had ever received by mail
measured_by: Hopkins/Bissell, counted orders from about 5,000 letters (about 1 in 5); no control group
family: old product renamed as a gift for a date
why: An article nobody wanted to restock got a new reason to be bought and a season, and the offer was a service, not a request to buy.
for_client: A cookware shop before Mother's Day: 'The Queen of Mother's Day Presents' on a free counter stand, offered only to shops that promise to display it.
source: Claude C. Hopkins, My Life in Advertising, Harper & Brothers, 1927, ch. "How I Got My Start in Advertising"
doubt: Own account written about 35 years later; no split with another letter. The first words of the letter itself are not printed; only the card line is.

opening: Bissell carpet sweepers are today offered twelve woods to the dozen, the twelve finest woods in the world.
picture: sweepers in twelve woods from white bird's-eye maple to dark walnut on a free rack
seller: Bissell Carpet Sweeper Company — carpet sweepers
beat: talking broom action, patent dumping devices, cyco bearings, which the directors wanted
result: sold our stock of 250,000 sweepers in three weeks
measured_by: Hopkins/Bissell sales; 250,000 sweepers; no control
family: last chance on a beautiful variety (true limit: never offered again)
why: It talked to women about a finish they could see and love instead of mechanics, and 'never be offered again' was literally true.
for_client: A kitchen-knife maker to shops: 'Our knives are today offered in twelve woods to the dozen, the twelve finest handles in the world. They will not be made again.' (only if true)
source: Claude C. Hopkins, My Life in Advertising, Harper & Brothers, 1927, ch. "How I Got My Start in Advertising"
doubt: Own account; Hopkins prints the letter 'in effect as follows', so wording is his reconstruction.

opening: [Vermilion envelope addressed in white ink, vermilion letterhead; pamphlet with a rajah's head: the story of vermilion wood — government forests in India, convicts, elephants, the Ganges River and the Pullman car]
picture: rajah's head on a vermilion cover; forests, convicts, elephants, the Ganges, the Pullman car
seller: Bissell Carpet Sweeper Company — vermilion-wood sweepers
beat: earlier years of the company; mechanical talk about a new dumping device
result: The Bissell Carpet Sweeper Company made more money in the next six weeks than they had made in any year before
measured_by: company profit as told by Hopkins; 100,000 dealer letters, two million pamphlets printed; no control
family: exotic origin story of the material (curiosity)
why: The story was made to arouse curiosity, to bring women in to see the wood.
for_client: A flooring shop: a deep-red envelope, white handwriting, and inside 'This oak lay under a lake in Finland for 200 years. Come and see it.' (a true origin only)
source: Claude C. Hopkins, My Life in Advertising, Harper & Brothers, 1927, ch. "How I Got My Start in Advertising"
doubt: Own account; envelope, story, scarcity and dealer agreement all changed together, so the part of the envelope alone is not known.

opening: [half-page newspaper ads announcing the biggest cake in the world]
picture: a cake baked with Cotosuet, decorated and built as high as the room, in the bay window of a new store
beat: six weeks of ordinary advertising, in which sales 'hardly increased at all'
result: during the next week 105,000 people climbed four flights of stairs to that cake; Cotosuet was placed on a profit-paying basis in Chicago
measured_by: Hopkins; visitors counted 105,000 in one week; sales figure not given
family: the world's biggest (spectacle that proves the product)
why: No argument in the world can ever compare with one dramatic demonstration; every guesser of the weight had to buy a pail.
